rationale: Amihud (2002, Journal of Financial Markets) is a fully operationalized empirical asset-pricing paper with two pillars: (1) a Fama-MacBeth cross-section of monthly NYSE returns on lagged stock characteristics (ILLIQMA, BETA, R100, R100YR, lnSIZE, SDRET, DIVYLD) over 408 months 1964-1997 (Table 2, with variable summary statistics in Table 1); and (2) time-series predictive regressions of annual and monthly market/size-portfolio excess returns on expected and unexpected market illiquidity, 1964-1996 (Tables 3-4), plus a monthly specification augmented with lagged default and term yield premiums (Table 5). Data section (Section 2.2-2.3) specifies the source (CRSP daily and monthly files; one-year and one-month T-bill rates from the Federal Reserve Bank; BAA/AAA/long-Treasury/3M-Tbill yields from Basic Economics), the sample (NYSE stocks 1963-1997, with explicit admission criteria (i)-(iv) and Shumway (1997) delisting-return treatment), the variable formulas (ILLIQ eq. (1), AILLIQ eq. (3), ILLIQMA eq. (4), Scholes-Williams portfolio betas eq. (5), AR(1) illiquidity model eq. (7) with Kendall (1954) bias correction, models (10), (10sz), (10m)), and the estimation windows. All five tables report coefficients, t-statistics, R-squared and Durbin-Watson statistics. Every required series is constructible from CRSP plus standard publicly available T-bill and bond-yield series.
